kicker: Electronics manufacturing · Q2 FY27 sales and margins
title: EMS sales surged, but margins fell at four of seven
title_em: margins fell at four of seven
dek: Much of the growth was dearer memory and metals passed on at cost: Dixon's phone and laptop prices rose 35–40% on flat volumes. Syrma grew 74% while its margin slipped to 9.7%.

chart.title: Revenue growth, Q2 FY27 vs Q2 FY26
chart.sub: consolidated revenue · label shows growth and change in EBITDA margin · bar colour = margin up or down

stats.label: Rise in Dixon's selling prices
stats.note: Phones and laptops, as memory got dearer; unit volumes stayed broadly flat.

stats.label: Syrma's margin on 74% growth
stats.note: 9.7% from 10.1%; FY27 margin guide cut to 10–10.5% as costs pass through.

stats.label: Centum's circuit-board lead time
stats.note: Up from 8–12 weeks; memories, controllers and capacitors are also short.

read: Pass-through makes revenue look bigger than profit; watch whether margins recover in FY28 as PCB and display plants start.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 20 Nov 2026
notes: Revenue growth and EBITDA margins from filed Q2 FY27 consolidated results (Centum's results are standalone, which now equals consolidated after its overseas exit). Amber and PG Electroplast are taken from their calls because the desk holds no consolidated filing: Amber 4.8% vs 5.9% (operating EBITDA ₹127 cr, +30%, on revenue ₹2,627 cr vs ₹1,647 cr); PG Electroplast 7.4% vs 6.8% (EBITDA ₹69.1 cr vs ₹44.7 cr, revenue +42.5%). Dixon is left out of the chart because only its small standalone filing is on the desk. Kaynes' fall is mainly from cutting smart-meter sales to collect dues, and Cyient DLM's from expensing sales spend, not pass-through.
